sections.h2: What does the Summit County Recorder Division do?
sections.html:
It records and preserves documents that touch real estate in Summit County. The Recorder Division sits inside the Fiscal Office, so the same elected Fiscal Officer who bills property tax also oversees recording. Deeds, mortgages and liens make up the core, and the division also keeps partnership papers, zoning amendments, military discharges, living wills and medical powers of attorney.

Every record except military discharges is open to the public. Online search covers documents from 1988 forward, and an Index Book Archive Viewer reaches records from 1840 to 1988. The division says outright that it performs no title or property searches, which leaves that task to the buyer's title company. Staff post a turnaround of three to five working days.

The Fiscal Office moved its divisions to temporary quarters during renovation of the Ohio Building at 175 S. Main St. in Akron. Call the division, or write recorder@summitoh.net, before delivering paper to a counter.

sections.h2: How does a Summit County deed get from signature to the record?
sections.html:
A deed passes through the Fiscal Office's transfer desk first and the recording desk second. The sequence below follows the Fiscal Office's property transfer page and its recording guide.

  1. The grantor signs, and the signing is acknowledged before a notary or another listed official under R.C. 5301.01.
  2. Bring the deed and the conveyance fee statement, DTE Form 100, or the exemption statement, DTE Form 100 (EX), to the Property Transfer Department. It approves the legal description and the conveyance.
  3. Deliver by 3:30 in the afternoon if you want the transfer completed on the same business day.
  4. Take the approved deed to the Recorder Division, with recording fees on their own check.

The guide wants legible pages, typed names under every signature, the complete legal description on first recordings, citations to earlier recorded documents, a return address with a phone number, numbered exhibits and a stamped return envelope.

Several e-recording vendors work with the office: Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners Network.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees for a deed in Summit County?
sections.html:
Summit County recording and transfer fees as posted on the Fiscal Office fee page
ChargePosted amount
Basic recording$34.00 covers the first two pages; $8.00 per page after
Non-compliant document$20.00 per document
Cross reference$4.00 each
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 of price, with the price stepped up to the next $100
Lot fee50 cents per lot in the legal description, exempt or not
Certification$1.00 per document

Fees come from R.C. 317.32. Read together, the statute splits the first two pages into a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fee, adds $4 and $4 for every later page, and allows a county to tack on a preservation surcharge of as much as $5. Summit's page lists $34 and $8 and shows no surcharge line, so confirm the exact total with the Recording Division first.

The division's FAQ prices a mailed copy of a deed at $4, with $1 more to certify it. The functions page lists $2 per page for copies. Military discharges go on record free.

sections.h2: Who pays the conveyance fee, and does Summit add a transfer tax?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. R.C. 319.202 has the grantee submit a value statement while the grantor covers the fee. For a sale, value means the full consideration paid or to be paid, mortgage balances and vendor's liens included. Gifts are measured by estimated open-market price, and knowingly misstating value is prohibited.

Ohio also lets counties adopt a real property transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100 under R.C. 322.02. Summit's fee page shows the conveyance fee and the lot fee, nothing more. Ask the Property Transfer Department whether any further charge reaches your deed.

A rental house carries one extra step: the auditor's endorsement tells the buyer to file rental information under R.C. 5323.02.

sections.h2: Which liens and releases can appear on a Summit County record?
sections.html:
The Recorder Division files mortgages and liens that bear on title, so a title company's search can turn up items recorded here. The fee page prices several of them:

  • IRS lien: $5.00. IRS release: $3.00.
  • Workers' compensation lien and its release: no fee.
  • Unemployment lien: no fee. Its release: $4.00.
  • Plats: $0.05 per square inch, with posted sizes running from $40.00 for 11 by 17 inches to $86.40 for 24 by 36 inches.
  • Township zoning regulations: $50.00. Township zoning amendments: $20.00.

Uniform Commercial Code filings carry their own fees, and the page sends callers to 330-643-8143.

Ask your title company for the recording reference of anything it finds. The recording guide asks submitters to cite earlier documents by number, by book and page, or by recording date.

sections.h2: How does a recorded deed connect to the Summit County tax bill?
sections.html:
The deed decides whose name lands on the next bill, and the county handles the two jobs in the same office. A few details from the Fiscal Office pages matter around closing:

  • Bills show the legal owner's name, and a bill covers the prior year because Ohio collects real estate tax one year in arrears.
  • A change to the mailing address on a tax bill must come in writing from the taxpayer to the Fiscal Officer. Recording a deed does not replace that request.
  • The owner-occupancy reduction ends when the property transfers, so a buyer who will live there applies on their own.
  • The conveyance statement asks the seller whether the home currently receives a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction.

Ask the title company to pull the current tax balance from the Treasurer division before the deed goes in for recording, so any open amount is settled at the table. The Summit tax certificate lien page says a lien sale is avoided by paying in full or entering a payment plan with the Delinquent Tax Department.

sections.h2: How do I fix a name or get a copy of a Summit County deed?
sections.html:
A recorded deed cannot be edited. The FAQ says a new deed must be prepared and recorded to change a name, and that only the person asking for the change or an attorney may prepare it. The new deed then goes back through the Property Transfer Department for the legal description and transfer before recording.

If you cannot find your own deed, request a copy by mail. Birth and death certificates are not kept here. Summit County Public Health issues them. The Veterans Service Commission helps with a lost DD 214 that was never recorded.

The office also mentions that a tax bill's mailing address changes only by written request from the taxpayer to the Fiscal Officer, which is separate from anything on the deed.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Summit County itself?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 538,376 residents for 2025 and 250,438 housing units, with median household income of $71,622. Owners occupy 67.5 percent of homes, and the middle owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 sits at $208,700. Median gross rent is $1,026.

Akron is the seat, and Wikipedia notes that the Fiscal Officer exercises the duties of auditor, treasurer and recorder. In a sale, the legal description check, the conveyance statement and the recording therefore all run through one county office.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Summit County?
faqs.a: The Recorder Division posts three to five working days. The Property Transfer Department can finish the transfer step the same business day when forms arrive by 3:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Is e-recording offered for Summit County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fiscal Office works with Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners Network, and title companies commonly file that way.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder run a title search for me?
faqs.a: No. The division says it performs no title or property searches. Your title company or attorney handles that.

faqs.q: Who can prepare a replacement deed to change a name?
faqs.a: Only the person requesting the change or an attorney. The new deed is recorded after the Property Transfer Department approves it.

faqs.q: Which Summit County records cannot be viewed online?
faqs.a: Military discharges. Recorded documents from 1988 forward show on the website, and older index books from 1840 to 1988 open in the archive viewer.
